LESSON: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Features of style

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 14.4.1 Features of style
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used. Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text
2. use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context
3. appreciate the importance of style in a work of art

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 14.4.1 Features of style

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 14.4.1 Features of style

Teach
• Focus skill: identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 14.4.1 Features of style
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used. Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
